applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 to identify transformer locations and proximity to parking/traffic areas. Transformer 2, located on the eastern side between Bldg. 4 and 5, is positioned directly adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation. The vision analysis confirmed this transformer sits within a few inches of the nearest parking space. No 20-foot all-weather access route is shown extending from the transformer pad to provide alternative access if the 6-foot threshold is exceeded. Access to this transformer depends entirely on proximity to the main paved driveway loop with no separate dedicated truck access route.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require transformer pads to be located within 6 feet of a drivable surface or parking/traffic area, OR if greater than 6 feet away, a 20-foot all-weather access route must be provided. Transformer 2 is clearly within 6 feet of parking (approximately 2 feet), which meets the first condition. However, the vision analysis of Sheet 9 indicates the transformer is located in a confined landscape island between parking and the driveway with no separate access easement or dedicated truck route. The requirement implies that Austin Energy trucks must have direct, unobstructed access to reach the transformer pad. The current configuration shows the pad accessible only via parking lot navigation or via the main driveway, neither of which is documented as a dedicated access route. While the distance technically satisfies the 6-foot requirement, the lack of any dedicated access documentation and the tight confinement of the pad suggest the intent of the requirement (to ensure reliable truck access) may not be met.
findings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is located directly adjacent to parking with less than 2 feet of clearance. Site plan does not show a dedicated 20-foot all-weather truck access route for this transformer. Provide either: (1) a documented dedicated truck access easement at least 20 feet long to the transformer pad, or (2) demonstrated coordination with Austin Energy confirming the parking lot access is acceptable for transformer truck operations.

applicableAreas: Entire site - all transformer pads (T2 and T3 inside gated property perimeter)
Main entrance driveway and property gates
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 site plan which shows an 'Entrance Gate' and 'Exit Gate' at the western property boundary on Valley View Road. Vision analysis identified that Transformer 1 and Transformer 4 are located at or near the entrance gate line, while Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) and Transformer 3 (southeastern corner, south of Bldg. 6) are located deep within the gated property perimeter. The site plan shows a residential condominium development (39 units, 8 buildings per facts.md) with controlled entry access via gates. Austin Energy personnel would require gate access codes or keys to reach T2 and T3, preventing 24/7 unrestricted emergency access.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 and § 1.11.1 explicitly require that all Austin Energy electrical equipment (including transformer pads) be accessible 24 hours per day, 7 days per week for emergency response and maintenance operations. The controlling provision states 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations' and requires 'Access to AE Facilities' without restriction. Gated residential communities with restricted access prevent Austin Energy trucks from having immediate, unrestricted 24/7 entry to reach transformer equipment during emergencies or for routine maintenance. When transformers are located within a gated property perimeter, Austin Energy requires either: (1) external placement of the transformer outside the gate line with direct truck access, (2) a permanent easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 access regardless of gate status, or (3) a documented AE Design exception authorizing the gated configuration with specific operational procedures. None of these alternatives are documented on the submitted plans.
findings.comment: Site plan shows entrance and exit gates controlling access to the property. Transformers 2 and 3 are located inside the gated perimeter, preventing 24/7 Austin Energy truck access for emergency response and maintenance. Provide: (1) evidence that all transformers are relocated outside the gated perimeter with direct unrestricted access from Valley View Road, OR (2) a recorded easement document providing Austin Energy unlimited 24/7 property access regardless of gate status, OR (3) documented written approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing gated access with emergency procedures.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad 1 (western edge, adjacent to Bldg. 2)
Tree well and landscaping area near Transformer 1
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 9 and 21 to identify site features near transformer pads. Transformer 1, located on the far western edge north of the main entrance driveway, is positioned directly adjacent to a labeled 'Tree Well' on Sheet 9. Vision analysis confirmed this transformer pad 'directly abuts a labeled Tree Well to its north.' Tree wells are protective structures around tree trunks that prevent direct vehicle access and movement. Additional overlapping tree canopy symbols were noted on Sheet 21 in the vicinity of T1. The transformer pad is surrounded by landscape elements that would restrict truck maneuvering and equipment placement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 and § 1.3.16 require that transformer pads 'be kept clear of all structures, landscaping, and improvements' to ensure Austin Energy personnel can install, operate, and maintain equipment with appropriate vehicle and personnel access. 'Trees, landscaping, street furniture, dumpster enclosures, water meters, grates, poles, fire hydrants' and other obstructions cannot block access to transformer pads or create safety hazards during equipment servicing. A tree well directly adjacent to the transformer pad represents a site feature that physically obstructs the clear zone and restricts the space available for truck approach, equipment landing, and personnel movement. Tree wells are designed to limit access to protect tree roots; this directly conflicts with the unrestricted access requirement for electrical equipment.
findings.comment: Transformer pad 1 is directly adjacent to a tree well, which obstructs access and creates a site feature blocking the required clear zone around the transformer. Remove the tree well or relocate the transformer to a site location that is free of landscaping, trees, tree wells, and other obstructions within a minimum 20 ft × 35 ft clear set-up area. Alternatively, provide documented coordination with Austin Energy Design and the arborist confirming the tree well can be modified or removed to provide unobstructed transformer access.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad 4 (southwestern side, west of Bldg. 8) and vicinity
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which shows Transformer 4 in the southwestern portion of the site (west of Bldg. 8). Vision analysis of this sheet identified that 'immediately adjacent to this pad is a dashed rectangle labeled "Vault Easement", suggesting below-grade infrastructure may be associated with this specific location.' The notation of a 'Vault Easement' indicates the applicant intends or is planning for vault infrastructure at this location. Per facts.md, the property address (3759 Valley View Road, Austin, TX 78704) is in South Austin, MF-2 zoning, and there is NO notation of the site being in the 'Network Area.' The facts.md specifically confirms: 'Regulating Plan: None' and the site address and zoning clearly place this property outside the downtown Network Area defined in UCM § 1.11.5.
findings.reasoning: The notation of 'Vault Easement' adjacent to Transformer 4 indicates an intent to construct or provide access to underground vault infrastructure. Per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5, transformer vault rooms are only permitted within the downtown Network Area. The property is clearly outside the Network Area (South Austin location, Valley View Road, MF-2 zoning). Therefore, vault room construction is prohibited at this location. The applicant must either: (1) remove the vault easement notation and confirm all transformers are pad-mounted only, or (2) if a vault is intended, relocate the infrastructure to a property within the downtown Network Area.
findings.comment: Sheet 21 shows a 'Vault Easement' notation adjacent to Transformer 4, indicating proposed vault infrastructure. The property is located outside the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5) where vault rooms are prohibited. Transformers outside the Network Area must be pad-mounted or in niches with AE Design consultation. Clarify: (1) Remove the Vault Easement notation if transformers will be pad-mounted, or (2) If a vault is intended, this site does not qualify per UCM § 1.5.2.6 and § 1.11.5 and cannot proceed with vault design at this location.

applicableAreas: Multiple buildings and meter locations throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) to trace visual line-of-sight paths from transformer pads to meter locations. Vision analysis confirmed: 'Because the meters are distributed on multiple exterior sides of the buildings (e.g., east and west walls) and the transformers are located at specific single points near the drive aisle, many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source. Therefore, many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer.' The four transformer pads are positioned at single points along the main drive loop (T1 west of Bldg. 2, T2 between Bldg. 4-5, T3 south of Bldg. 6, T4 west of Bldg. 8), while meters are distributed on multiple building faces (east side, west side, south side). Building structures physically obstruct the visual path from many meters to their source transformers.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 (Location of Meter Sockets) requires transformers to be 'within sight' of meter locations to enable Austin Energy personnel to 'verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' The Regulatory Overview for this grouping clarifies: 'Transformers must be within line of sight of meters to enable AE personnel to verify equipment connections and perform coordinated operations.' Line of sight means an unobstructed visual path - if a building structure blocks the direct view from meter to transformer, the line of sight requirement is not met. The vision analysis explicitly identified that 'many meters are on the opposite side of the building from their likely power source,' which necessarily means building structures obstruct the line of sight. AE personnel cannot verify connections and perform coordinated operations if they cannot see both the meter and the transformer from a single vantage point.
findings.comment: Many meter locations on building faces do not have direct unobstructed line of sight to transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path. Meters on the east/west/south sides of buildings cannot see transformers on opposite sides. Provide: (1) Confirmation that all meters are relocated to faces that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer, OR (2) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units authorizing the non-line-of-sight meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing path from transformers to meters throughout site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to trace electrical routing paths and count 90-degree bends. Vision analysis traced 'the primary electrical routing is denoted by a solid blue line. It enters the site from the mid-western boundary... splits to form a continuous underground loop that follows the inner perimeter of the internal drive aisle, circling the central buildings.' The analysis specifically identified: 'There are numerous 90-degree bends. Counting just the primary main loop (excluding small jogs to individual pads/meters), there are at least 6 distinct 90-degree corners to navigate the rectangular layout of the site.' The primary electrical loop makes a rectangular circuit around the central buildings, requiring approximately 6 90-degree directional changes (one at each corner of the rectangular loop). Branch connections from this main loop to individual transformers and meters add additional turns.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q (Current Transformers and Enclosures) specifies 'maximum two 90-degree turns in electrical routing between transformer pad and meter.' This limitation is imposed to maintain circuit performance and prevent voltage drop issues. The vision analysis conclusively identified at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary electrical routing loop, which is triple the maximum allowable. The rectangular main loop circuit requires a 90-degree bend at each corner (north, east, south, west), and the perimeter-following design necessitates these turns. This configuration cannot be reconfigured without a complete redesign of the electrical routing topology. The current design violates the maximum two-turn requirement.
findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 contains at least 6 distinct 90-degree turns in the primary underground electrical loop, exceeding the maximum of 2 turns permitted by UCM § 1.9.1.9.Q. The rectangular loop configuration around the central buildings necessitates multiple directional changes. Revise the electrical routing design to limit turns between transformer pads and meters to a maximum of two 90-degree bends, or provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing the exceeding the standard 2-turn limitation for this site configuration.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing near Transformers 1, 2, 3, 4 and associated drainage infrastructure
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21, 9, and 12 to identify proximity of electrical routing to drainage infrastructure. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted: 'Drainage: There is an underground storm drain network (marked with dashed lines and SD) running parallel to the electrical lines in several places, particularly close to the routing near Bldg. 8 and Bldg. 4/5.' Vision analysis of Sheet 9 identified: 'T1 has Wastewater Easement nearby; T2 and T3 have Storm Drain lines adjacent; T4 has Wastewater Easement nearby.' The site plan shows utility lines for water (W), storm drain (SD), and wastewater (WW) running throughout the property. However, no specific clearance dimensions or separation distances are provided on any of the sheets. Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) shows 24-inch and 18-inch HDPE storm drain pipes with specific elevations and profiles, but these details do not correlate with specific electrical routing clearance measurements on Sheet 21.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5 (Clearances for AE Underground Cable, Conduit, and Underground Facilities) specifies 'minimum 12-inch clearance to other utilities.' The code citation language allows for interpretation - the minimum 12-inch clearance standard applies, but operational practice (referenced in the grouping as 'operational practice may require 5 feet for drainage infrastructure') may impose stricter separation for compatibility. Without specific clearance dimensions shown on the electrical plan or correlated details between electrical routing and drainage infrastructure profiles, it cannot be definitively determined whether the 12-inch minimum (or operationally appropriate 5-foot) clearance is maintained. The visual proximity noted by the vision analysis (routing 'very close' to drainage lines) suggests potential inadequate clearance, but cannot be confirmed without detailed profile views or cross-section details showing the vertical and horizontal separation distances between electrical conduits and drainage pipes.
findings.comment: Electrical routing shown on Sheet 21 is located adjacent to wastewater easements (T1, T4) and storm drain infrastructure (T2, T3), but no specific clearance dimensions are documented. Overlay Sheet 21 electrical routing with Sheet 12 drainage infrastructure details to verify minimum 12-inch clearance from drainage facilities. Provide cross-section details or a coordinate overlay demonstrating that electrical conduit maintains adequate clearance from all drainage infrastructure, or provide documentation from Austin Energy confirming acceptable separation distances for this site configuration.

applicableAreas: Transformer equipment specifications and vault design (if applicable)
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and the Engineer's Summary Letter supplementary document. Block 3 of Sheet 21 drawing shows 'electrical elements such as transformers, pull boxes, underground electric lines, and electrical meters' but provides no equipment specifications. The blocks.md for Sheet 21 explicitly states: 'None are provided on this sheet. The items are generically labeled Electrical Transformer Pad.' No electrical engineering report, load calculations, transformer kVA ratings, voltage specifications, phase information, or ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form references are provided in any of the submitted documents. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary doc) addresses only water and wastewater utilities, with no mention of electrical load calculations or transformer specifications. No transformer count is documented anywhere on the submitted plans.
findings.reasoning: Without load calculations and transformer specifications, Austin Energy Design and Network Design cannot verify that the proposed electrical infrastructure is adequate for the development's power requirements. The design is incomplete per UCM § 1.11.1 and cannot proceed to construction without this essential information.
findings.comment: No electrical engineering load calculations, transformer specifications, or ESPA form reference are provided on Sheet 21 or in supplementary documents. Provide: (1) Complete electrical engineering calculations including transformer count, kVA ratings, voltage classes, and amperage specifications for all proposed transformers, (2) ESPA (Electrical System Project Application) form completed and submitted to Austin Energy Network Design, (3) Final voltage and load documentation confirming the proposed equipment meets the development's power requirements and complies with Austin Energy standards.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad 2 (eastern location, between Bldg. 4 and 5, adjacent to parking)
findings.observation: Examined Sheets 21 and 9 to identify transformer pad locations and proximity to parking areas. Transformer 2 (eastern side, between Bldg. 4 and 5) is positioned immediately adjacent to a surface parking space with less than 2 feet of separation per vision analysis: 'T2 is located directly adjacent to a perpendicular surface parking space. It appears to share a boundary or sit mere inches from the northernmost parking space in the cluster west of Bldg. 5. It is absolutely within 6 feet of this parking space.' No bollard symbols or notations are shown on Sheet 21 or Sheet 9 at this transformer location. Sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) was not reviewed but would be the expected location for bollard specifications if they were required and shown elsewhere on the plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Bollard requirement when transformer pad is within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas... 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards are required and must be spaced to allow equipment door opening.' When transformer equipment is installed less than or equal to 4 feet from a parking space or traffic area, bollards must be provided to prevent vehicles from striking and damaging the transformer. Transformer 2 is less than 2 feet from a parking space, well within the 4-foot trigger distance. This proximity to parking makes the transformer vulnerable to vehicle impact and also creates a safety hazard for parked vehicles in an adjacent space that is separated only by the thin equipment pad. Bollards serve a dual purpose: (1) protecting the transformer from vehicle damage, and (2) preventing vehicles from parking or maneuvering too close to the electrical equipment. The absence of bollards at T2 violates this requirement.
findings.comment: Transformer pad 2 is positioned less than 2 feet from a surface parking space, triggering the bollard requirement per UCM § 1.10.4. No bollards are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide: (1) Detail drawing for 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards (per UCM § 1.10.4 standard specification) positioned around Transformer 2, with spacing adequate to allow equipment door openings and access (minimum 3-foot clear width for door swing), OR (2) Reposition Transformer 2 to a location more than 4 feet from all parking spaces and traffic areas.

applicableAreas: All four transformer pads (T1, T2, T3, T4) relative to adjacent sidewalks and pedestrian paths
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) to measure distance from transformer pads to sidewalks and pedestrian paths. Vision analysis identified clearances for each transformer: 'T1: A Concrete Sidewalk wraps tightly around the eastern and northern sides of this pad. It appears to be within 2 feet of the pad. T2: A concrete sidewalk running north-south along the side of Bldg. 4 passes very close to the western edge of this pad (appears to be within 2 feet). T3: A concrete walkway runs east-west just north of the pad, connecting the driveway to Unit 604. It appears to be within 2 to 5 feet. T4: A concrete sidewalk runs north-south just to the east of the pad, leading to Unit 801. It appears to be within 2 feet.' Three of the four transformers (T1, T2, T4) are documented as being within 2 feet of sidewalks, which meets or may slightly exceed the 2-foot minimum. T3 is within 2-5 feet. No specific dimension lines, callouts, or clearance annotations are provided on the site plan to document compliance with the 2-foot setback requirement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 specifies: 'Transformer equipment pads not minimum 2 feet from back of sidewalks.' The 'back of sidewalk' refers to the edge of the sidewalk surface farthest from the roadway or pedestrian area - essentially the inner edge of the sidewalk adjacent to property features. A 2-foot minimum separation is required to: (1) provide space for sidewalk maintenance and repair, (2) prevent sidewalk deterioration from transformer vibration or equipment settling, (3) ensure pedestrians are not placed in direct proximity to electrical equipment, and (4) allow for minor adjustments in sidewalk alignment during maintenance. Vision analysis indicates T1, T2, and T4 are at or potentially at less than the 2-foot minimum. While T3 may be within acceptable range (2-5 feet is unclear - 'within 2 to 5 feet' could mean 2 feet or could mean 5 feet). The absence of specific dimension documentation on the site plan creates ambiguity. To comply with the requirement, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate the 2-foot setback is maintained. Estimated visual distances are insufficient for compliance verification.
findings.comment: Multiple transformer pads appear to be located within 2 feet of concrete sidewalks per visual analysis of Sheet 9. Provide: (1) Updated site plan with dimension lines and callouts clearly documenting the distance from back of sidewalk to each transformer pad (T1, T2, T3, T4), confirming minimum 2-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.4, OR (2) Reposition transformers to achieve minimum 2-foot separation from all sidewalks, or (3) If clearance cannot be achieved, provide documented approval from Austin Energy Design authorizing reduced sidewalk clearance with specific approval conditions.

applicableAreas: Multiple meter locations throughout the site
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 to identify meter locations and access. Vision analysis identified: 'Locations: Meters are explicitly labeled as Electrical Meters using text boxes with leader lines. The leader lines point directly to the exterior walls of the buildings. Locations include: West side of Bldg. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8; East side of Bldg. 1, 2, 4, 6, 8; South side of Bldg. 7.' All meters appear to be exterior wall-mounted locations with no indication on Sheet 21 that any meters are behind doors, in enclosed rooms, or elevated above ground level. Standard notation on electrical plans would explicitly indicate 'Meter Room' or location callouts if meters were not directly accessible. The notations appear to place meters on first-floor/ground-level building faces.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 addresses 'Meters shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer, without written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units documented.' Two alternative compliance paths exist: (1) Meters are on first floor/ground level AND within sight of transformer (standard requirement), OR (2) Meters are not on first floor/ground level OR not within sight of transformer (exception scenario that requires written approval). The deficiency statement in EL-14.70 specifically addresses the exception case: 'when meters are shown not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer.' This triggers if either condition is not met. Vision analysis from EL-14.38 documented that 'many meters do NOT have a direct line of sight to a transformer' because they are on opposite sides of buildings. This represents a failure of the 'within sight' requirement. The Regulatory Overview clarifies the requirement: 'Meter locations not on first floor/ground level or not within sight of transformer require written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units.' The submitted plans show many meters without line of sight but provide no documented approval from AE Design or Distribution Metering. Therefore, EL-14.70 is a fail.
findings.comment: Many meter locations shown on Sheet 21 are not within sight of transformer pads due to building structures blocking the visual path (see EL-14.38 findings). Provide: (1) Documented written approval from Austin Energy Design AND Distribution Metering business units authorizing meter locations without direct line of sight to transformers, OR (2) Reposition all meters to locations that have direct, unobstructed visual line of sight to their source transformer on first floor/ground level per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
